title: Which engine serves each repo
intro: Already fixed: a run keeps its own copy of the kit (workflows, rules, schemas) from the day it was created. Asked: which engine program should carry out commands for a repo on an older or newer kit.

decisions.title: Which engine serves each repo
decisions.question: When two of your repos are on different kit versions, should each one's commands run on the engine that came with its own kit?
decisions.today: Every command, for every repo, runs on the one engine installed next to the factory command. I put a stand-in engine inside a test repo's factory folder and ran a status command: it printed the installed engine's answer, "0 run(s)", and the stand-in never ran. A repo's own factory folder holds no engine at all, because factory init leaves that folder out.
decisions.after: With the recommended option, factory init and factory upgrade copy the engine into the repo's factory folder. A run started on that kit keeps using that engine until it ends, even after you upgrade the factory command, and two repos on different kits each run their own.
decisions.preview:
Your repo's factory folder after factory init (today, from a test run):
  factory/dashboard  languages  policies  schemas  shims  skills  skills.lock
  factory/stages.map.yaml  workflows  launcher

After the recommended option, the same listing gains one folder:
  factory/engine/factory_engine   (58 source files, about 1.4 MB)

Commands for this repo then run that engine, not the one installed next to the factory command.

options.name: Each repo brings its own engine
options.see: Each repo's factory folder carries its own copy of the engine, and a run keeps the engine it was created with.
options.asks: Nothing new to do. The repo's factory folder gets about 1.4 MB larger (58 files) the next time you run factory init or factory upgrade, and that change is committed with the rest of the kit.
options.how: The launcher points Python at the kit's engine folder before it starts an engine. The libraries the engine needs (PyYAML, jsonschema) still come from the launcher's own install.
pros: Matches the spec: a repo on an older kit never runs newer engine code against its older workflows
Testable now: two repos with two stand-in engines, and each answers for itself
A run in progress is not changed by upgrading the factory command
cons: Every target repo commits a copy of the engine's source
Libraries are still shared, so two kits that need different library versions would clash
factory init and factory upgrade change, so repos already set up need one upgrade

options.name: Each kit gets its own full Python environment
options.see: Each kit version is run in its own private Python environment, with its own engine and its own pinned libraries.
options.asks: A wait the first time each kit version runs, while its environment is built, and the kit must carry a pinned list of libraries (it has none today).
options.how: A virtual environment is built from the kit's requirements.lock the first time a snapshot runs, and its interpreter starts the engine.
pros: Matches the spec word for word, including keeping libraries apart between kits
No clash if one kit needs newer libraries than another
cons: The pinned library list does not exist yet, so it must be written and kept up to date
A first-run wait and extra disk for every kit version
Much bigger than what the open criterion needs

options.name: Keep one engine for everything
options.see: Nothing changes: one engine serves every repo, and the written promise about per-repo engines is dropped for phase 1a.
options.asks: Keep every repo on the same factory version as the installed command, and upgrade them together.
options.how: The criterion is marked not applicable and module 16's text is changed to say one engine serves all repos.
pros: No engine source copied into target repos
cons: A repo on an older kit runs newer engine code against its older workflows, which the kit design forbids
Upgrading the factory command changes runs already in progress
The criterion is dropped instead of met

decisions.why: It is the smallest change that makes each repo run its own engine and keeps a running run on the engine it started with, without the pinned-library work the full environment option needs.
